artists.biography: Cynthia "Cindy" Leigh Wilson is a singer, songwriter, and a founding member of new wave rock band The B-52s. The B-52's were formed when Wilson, alongside her older brother and guitarist Ricky, organist and vocalist Kate Pierson, drummer and percussionist Keith Strickland, and vocalist Fred Schneider played an impromptu musical jam session after sharing a tropical Flaming Volcano drink at a local Chinese restaurant. They later played their first concert in 1977 at a Valentine's Day party for their friends. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Change is Cindy Wilson's debut solo album, released in December 2017 through the independent label Kill Rock Stars. The record showcases a significant stylistic departure from her work with The B-52's, embracing synth-pop, dance, and electronica with a low-tempo, melodic approach. Produced by Suny Lyons and recorded at The Space Station in Athens, Georgia, the album features ten tracks comprising eight original compositions and two covers—New Colony Six's "Things I'd Like to Say" and Oh-OK's "Brother."

The album marked the culmination of several years of collaborative work between Wilson and her solo band, initially developed for live performances before evolving into a more structured recording project. Crowdfunded through PledgeMusic, Change represented Wilson's first full-length solo effort, following two self-released EPs: Sunrise (2016) and Supernatural (2017). While the album did not achieve commercial chart success, critics responded positively to Wilson's exploration of psychedelic electronic music and synth-driven pop, with the record earning a 74% positive score on Metacritic. An official music video was released for the track "Brother," further promoting the album's electronic-focused aesthetic.
